blocks.text: 很少有地方比日本更看重这种本地化的细微差别。日语句子不一定都有主语和宾语，用词会随交谈对象而变化。道歉很常见，因为道歉几乎不承担什么责任；停顿表达的是思考，而非尴尬。受到称赞时通常会推辞，直接说“不”往往也会回避。日语里甚至有个说法叫 kūki o yomu，即“读空气”，意思是人们应当领会那些没有说出口的话。

blocks.text: “要让 AI 的价值惠及每一个人，与 AI 的交互就必须自然、直观，”ElevenLabs 联合创始人兼 CEO Mati Staniszewski 表示。“人们所说的语言和遵循的社会规范，必须从一开始就体现在技术的架构之中。Kotoba 在日本正是这样做的，他们打造的顶尖语音模型已被一些全球领先企业采用。携手合作，我们可以更进一步，为日本的 AI 构建完整的交互层。”

blocks.text: “创立 Kotoba 时，我们的目标是在日本打造一家前沿 AI 实验室，”Kotoba Technologies, Inc. 联合创始人兼 CEO Noriyuki Kojima 表示。“一路走来，我们看到了语音 AI 的巨大潜力；三年后的今天，我们比以往任何时候都更坚定地要打造造福社会的技术。Kotoba 加入 ElevenLabs，让我无比兴奋。携手合作，我们可以加速语音 AI 的研发与普及，为日本乃至全球的个人和企业带来实实在在的好处。”

blocks.text: Kojima（大家叫他 Nori）拥有康奈尔大学计算机科学博士学位。他曾在 Hugging Face 担任研究科学家，并参与打造了日本的 Fugaku-LLM——一个在 RIKEN Fugaku 超级计算机上从零训练的开源模型。Kasai 拥有华盛顿大学计算机科学与工程博士学位，曾任芝加哥大学丰田技术研究所助理教授。他是日本被引用次数最多的研究者之一。

blocks.text: The way we speak and interact with each other is deeply local. We talk in different languages, dialects, and accents, and our behavior is governed by a complex, often unstated, mix of local social and cultural norms.

inlines.text: The way we speak and interact with each other is deeply local. We talk in different languages, dialects, and accents, and our behavior is governed by a complex, often unstated, mix of local social and cultural norms.

blocks.text: There are few places where local nuance is more important than in Japan. Sentences don’t always contain a subject and an object, and vocabulary changes depending on who you’re speaking to. Apologies are common because they carry little liability, and pauses signal thought rather than awkwardness. Praise is typically deflected, and saying “no” directly is often avoided. Japanese even has a phrase, kūki o yomu, or “reading the air,” which means people are expected to pick up what isn’t said.

blocks.text: Our goal is to solve how people interact with AI in every language and culture. That means building AI that feels natural and intuitive across different cultures and contexts, so everyone can access and benefit from it.

blocks.text: With deep voice research and knowledge of the Japanese market, the Kotoba team is a natural partner in this mission. The company was founded by AI researchers Noriyuki Kojima and Jungo Kasai in 2023, with the aim of developing voice AI for a multilingual world. As they put it, “Speech shouldn't stop where language does.”

blocks.text: “To bring the value of AI to every person, it needs to be natural and intuitive to interact with,” said Mati Staniszewski, co-founder and CEO of ElevenLabs. “The language people speak and the social norms they follow need to be reflected in the technology’s architecture from the very start. Kotoba has done exactly that for Japan, building state-of-the-art voice models that have already been adopted by some of the world’s leading enterprises. Together, we can take that even further together and build the full interaction layer for AI in Japan.”

blocks.text: “When we founded Kotoba, our goal was to build a frontier AI lab from Japan,” said Noriyuki Kojima, co-founder and CEO of Kotoba Technologies, Inc. “Along the way, we’ve seen the enormous potential of voice AI, and three years later, we’re more determined than ever to build technology that benefits society. I’m incredibly excited for Kotoba to join ElevenLabs. Together, we can accelerate the development and adoption of voice AI, bringing tangible benefits to people and businesses in Japan and beyond.”

blocks.text: Kojima, who goes by Nori, holds a PhD in computer science from Cornell. He worked as a research scientist at Hugging Face, and co-built Japan’s Fugaku-LLM, an open-source model trained from scratch on the RIKEN Fugaku supercomputer. Kasai holds a PhD in computer science and engineering from the University of Washington, and was an assistant professor at Toyota Technological Institute at the University of Chicago. He is one of Japan’s most-cited researchers.

blocks.text: Kotoba’s voice model, Koto, excels in Japanese text-to-speech, speech-to-text, and speech-to-speech for simultaneous interpretation. Several major global enterprises already use Koto, including Salesforce, where it powers Japanese-language conversations in Agentforce Voice. With Kotoba joining ElevenLabs, more of the world’s leading companies will be able to build agents that handle complex conversations in Japanese naturally.
